summary: Fix-verification follow-up to iteration_112. Built a new 14-test pytest suite (/app/backend/tests/test_iter113_fix_verification.py) — 14/14 passed — plus 5 Playwright runs on the public preview URL. ALL 5 FIXES VERIFIED: (1) GET /api/auth/me now returns must_change_password + mfa_enabled, and a freshly admin-created user logging in through the real UI now lands on /set-password (was /dashboard in iter112); (2) Settings > Security now shows a 'Disabled' badge + a visible 'Enable 2FA' button for BOTH admin and manager, no 'mandatory/cannot be disabled' copy, and with mfa_enabled=true it correctly flips to 'Enabled' + 'Disable 2FA' + OTP confirm step (full toggle round trip enable->disable exercised via UI + API, admin restored to mfa_enabled=false); (3) reset-password and change-password happy paths fully work (forgot -> reset -> old pw 401 -> new pw login -> change-password -> old pw 401 -> new pw login), supabase_password_set flips TRUE, weak (9-char) password rejected 400, wrong current_password rejected; (5) both /reset-password and /accept-invite now consistently say 10 characters (placeholder 'At least 10 characters' + minLength=10 on reset; 'Min. 10 characters' + inline 'Password must be at least 10 characters' on invite) — no '8 characters' copy anywhere on those two pages. Fix 4 (429/403 mapping) not testable without simulating Supabase rate-limiting — skipped as instructed. All iter112 regression scenarios re-pass. ONE ENVIRONMENT BLOCKER FOUND: the frontend has NO hot reload (frontend supervisor runs `yarn start` = `vite build && vite preview`), so the served bundle was a stale 11:07 build while the source fixes were 13:31 — Fix 2 and Fix 5 initially appeared UNFIXED in the browser until I ran `sudo supervisorctl restart frontend`. That is almost certainly why the main agent's own Playwright trace looked wrong.

minor.issue: VERIFIED FIXED — must_change_password and mfa_enabled now present and correctly typed (bool) for admin, manager, super_admin and a new admin-created user; no _id/password_hash leakage.

Happy path verified end to end. The new 503-on-Supabase-failure branch for already-migrated users could NOT be exercised (no way to simulate a Supabase-side write failure from the preview env) — code was read and looks correct, but it remains UNTESTED.

ui_bugs.issue: Dead code: super_admin can never reach this panel — /settings redirects super_admin to the Super Admin dashboard (only a 'Change password' item in the sidebar), so the isMandatory === 'super_admin' branch never renders. Fix 2(c) is therefore satisfied only vacuously; MFA mandatoriness for super_admin was confirmed at the API level (login returns requires_mfa:true, no access token). Either drop the branch or give super_admin a real security panel.
Password input has no minLength attribute (ResetPassword.js has minLength=10). Copy + JS validation are correct, only the native constraint is missing — cosmetic inconsistency.

design_issues.screen: Admin/manager password-set forms (NOT part of the 5 fixes)
issues: Password copy still says 8 characters while the backend enforces 10 in: components/admin/UsersTab.js:64,213 ('Min. 8 characters'), pages/SuperAdminDashboard.js:780, pages/OrgStructure.js:312,330,849, pages/PeopleHub.js:381. An admin typing a 9-char password there passes client validation and gets a 400 from the API. Same class of bug Fix 5 addressed — should be fixed for consistency.
The form renders fully for an obviously invalid token (?token=dummy) and only fails on submit; no upfront token validation like /accept-invite does. Pre-existing, low priority.

action_items: IMPORTANT WORKFLOW: the frontend does NOT hot-reload (yarn start = vite build && vite preview). Run `sudo supervisorctl restart frontend` (takes ~60s to rebuild) after every frontend source edit, otherwise you and the test agent both see the previous build. This is why your Playwright verification of Fix 2/Fix 5 failed.

Optional consistency follow-up: update the remaining '8 characters' password copy/validation in UsersTab.js, SuperAdminDashboard.js, OrgStructure.js, PeopleHub.js to 10 characters (see design_issues).
Optional: remove or repurpose the unreachable super_admin isMandatory branch in OrgSettings SecurityTab, and add minLength={10} to the AcceptInvite password input.
critical_code_review_comments: deps.get_current_user's explicit column allow-list remains a silent contract with the frontend — consider a shared constant / Pydantic response model so future user flags cannot silently disappear from /auth/me again (this was the root cause of iter112's must_change_password regression).

The 503 hardening in reset_password/change_password is inherently untestable in this environment; consider a dev-only env flag (e.g. SUPABASE_FORCE_FAIL) so the stranded-user path can be regression-tested.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Run `python3 -m pytest tests/test_iter113_fix_verification.py -n 0 -q` from /app/backend (~2 min; -n 0 required because the failed-login tests share the per-IP rate limiter — the suite clears login_attempts itself). Helper tests/_iter113_mfa_toggle.py enable|disable|state toggles admin MFA via the real API (bypasses OTP by writing bcrypt('123456') into users.mfa_code) and prints usable supervision_access/refresh cookies for Playwright cookie injection. tests/_iter112_ui_fixture.py purge <email> cleans Postgres + Supabase. REMEMBER: restart the frontend supervisor after any frontend source change — there is no hot reload. Still untested: the Supabase-outage 503 branch and the verify_login 429/403 mapping (Fix 4).
rca_of_the_issue: No new product defects. The only real finding is environmental: /app/frontend is served as a Vite production build (`yarn start` = `vite build && vite preview`), so source edits are invisible until the frontend supervisor process is restarted and rebuilds. The main agent's inability to confirm Fix 2/Fix 5 in the browser was caused by the browser being served the 11:07 build while the fixes landed at 13:31; after `supervisorctl restart frontend` all frontend fixes rendered correctly.
